description:
AUDITED at clean origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83 (2026-09-02).

## Goal

Every value admitted by a runtime-dispatch arm must be safe for the body behind that arm. When two emitted predicates overlap, dispatch must either:

1. distinguish the representation-relevant surfaces at runtime; or
2. avoid retaining separate bodies whose distinction the runtime predicate erases.

Arrival order, specificity order, and stress seed must never select a body compiled for an incompatible representation.

## Current state

fz-kdt.119 and fz-kdt.107 removed the ticket's original tuple and disjoint list-head populations. The old five-line list(:ok)/list(int) reproducer is now green on interp, JIT, and AOT because atom and integer heads ask disjoint questions.

The unresolved class is overlap without surface containment. In `callsite_dispatch::specificity_order`, `covers(early, late)` requires the early surface to contain the late surface wherever their predicates overlap on an erasing axis. If neither arm covers the other, the pair stays in arrival order. That is not a safe resolution: both orders can admit a value to a body whose representation did not name it.

The pinned settled-order census contains exactly three such list-tail pairs:

- dispatch_list_head_separates: `[:false | :true]` / `[int | :ok | :true]`
- enum_predicate_search: `[:false | :nil]` / `[int | :nil]`
- enum_predicate_search: `[:false | :true]` / `[int | :ok | :true]`

Those examples happen to use representation-compatible boxed element access today; that is not a proof of the general invariant.

A live representation-incompatible instance exists on the map-capture axis. One lambda is minted with either `%{a: float}` or `%{a: int}` and selected through mailbox-derived control flow before passing through `P.run/2`. The runtime callable questions retain the capture surfaces, but map predicates test only MAP kind. Both questions therefore admit both closure constructions, and arrival order chooses a body grounded for one capture representation.

Independent result at a3a9761d1:

- oracle: `11.0`, `12`
- interp: rc 0, `11.0`, `12.0`
- JIT: rc 134 after `11.0`; `fz_ref_load_float: expected Float, found Int`
- AOT: build rc 0; executable rc 134 with the same failure

Do not repair this by choosing the opposite order: reversing which capture arrives first produces the symmetric int/float misroute.

The fz-kdt.143 comment describes commit d2a5f3510 on `origin/wt/kdt-close`; that commit is not an ancestor of this audited main baseline. Re-census if it lands, but its documented redundant-arm drop does not resolve overlap-without-containment.

## Strategy

Start from the representation contract consumed by each specialized body. For every pair of runtime-dispatch alternatives whose predicates overlap, prove that any value admitted to the earlier body satisfies that body's representation contract. Where this cannot be proven:

- refine the runtime question to expose the needed distinction; or
- merge/generalize the semantic specialization before materialization.

Keep the predicate, interpreter lowering, native lowering, seating relation, and artifact representation contract derived from one model. Do not add an ordering exception.

## Signal

1. A three-door behavioral fixture for the mailbox-selected int/float map-capture witness.
2. Both int-first and float-first construction/arrival orders.
3. A unit-level invariant over dispatch plans: overlapping arms may not remain separate when their only distinction is erased but their body representation contracts are incompatible.
4. The blind-escape census run under settled order and whole-order arm seeds, reported by named pair rather than only a count.

## Acceptance

- The map-capture witness prints exactly `11.0` then `12` on interp, JIT, and AOT.
- The symmetric arrival-order witness prints exactly `12` then `11.0` on all three doors.
- No runtime-dispatch plan can route a value into a body whose representation contract excludes it.
- The three named list-tail residue pairs are either made distinguishable or proven representation-compatible by the same explicit invariant; they may not remain justified merely by current arrival order.
- `dispatch_seat_element_blind` remains green under settled order and all exercised arm permutations.
- Preserve statically known capture specialization: calls whose capture types are already separated by activation keys must not gain manufactured runtime dispatch.
- Update `callsite_dispatch` and dispatch-matrix documentation to remove the stale original-population account and state the representation-safety rule.
- Run focused unit tests, both arrival-order witnesses through all three doors, `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --lib`, and the fixture matrix.

comments.text: fz-kdt.119 review correction (2026-09-01): overlaps_on_an_erasing_axis's doc calls ints/floats exact ('a value passes only by being in the tested set, which the arm's surface names') -- but runtime_type_predicate stores ints/floats as PRESENCE BITS only and ignores descr.brands unless cofinite, so two arms with surfaces 'brand X of int' / 'brand Y of int' have EQUAL tests and incomparable surfaces, and covers declares the position non-erasing and seats freely. Benign today (brands are runtime-erased by design, reprs identical -- fz-bsx) but the doc claim is false as written and becomes a live hole if numeric singletons return (the predicate's own comment says they are recoverable from history). Correct the doc claim when this ticket or 119 next touches the file. ALSO: 119 partially unblocks this ticket (tuple pairs gain separation and leave the neither-covers population; LIST pairs do not -- the queue does not empty).

fz-kdt.119 LANDED (4ca1dc7e7). Three things here are now settled or measured.

1. THE DOC CLAIM IS CORRECTED, as this ticket's comment asked. overlaps_on_an_erasing_axis no longer says ints/floats are exact 'because a value passes only by being in the tested set, which the arm's surface names' -- that was false, since the projection stores them as PRESENCE BITS and ignores brands, so 'brand X of int' and 'brand Y of int' put the same question and hold incomparable surfaces. The classification (separating) is unchanged and the stated REASON is now the true one: every value the axis admits has ONE representation, brands being runtime-erased by construction (fz-bsx), so no admitted body can misread what arrives. The row also records that restoring numeric singletons re-opens it. The claim now lives in RuntimeTestAxis::precision, the one table three lowerings and this relation share.

2. THE TUPLE POPULATION LEAVES, THE LIST POPULATION DOES NOT, as this ticket predicted. A tuple pair is now judged position by position: erasing only where two shapes that could both admit a value overlap at a position that is ITSELF erasing. Measured consequence on the corpus: enum_predicate_search's List.reduce_while_step/3 pair stops needing coverage at all (both state positions are atoms) and precision re-seats it narrow-first -- the 28-line canon move in 119. The 19-escape census is UNMOVED, entry for entry, because every one of the 19 is a list subject; only fz-kdt.107 step 3 can move that number, exactly as this ticket's other comment said.

3. THE THIRD FACET ({A,B} vs {B,C} overlapping without containment) is untouched and still owned here. Re-census after fz-kdt.107 step 3, not before: the neither-covers population is what enum_map_family's 150 schedule-dependent arm lines sit in, and it is still arrival-decided.

Also relevant: the seating rule itself is unchanged. What changed underneath it is what 'the tests differ' is allowed to mean.

fz-kdt.107 step-3 review (2026-09-01): after Stage 2 lands, this ticket's facet-3 (overlap-without-containment) population is EXACTLY 2, both in enum_predicate_search, both named ([:false|:nil]/[int|:nil] and [:false|:true]/[int|:ok|:true]) -- arrival-kept, meaning-neutral today only because both arms are specializations of one source function with boxed element access (luck, ARGUED not proven). The cure for these two is nothing dispatch can do (heads overlap; tails erased); they wait on a repr-level or minting-level decision. Re-measure on landing.

fz-kdt.141: the neither-covers residue this ticket owns is now perturbable, and it is what the new stress moves.

The retired reversal knob mirrored WITHIN a question group only, so it never touched a cross-group pair -- your recorded gap ('the reversal stress does NOT exercise cross-group order -- fz-kdt.131 needs a cross-group permutation stress'). FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=arms:<seed> permutes the whole arrival order and then lets specificity_order do its deterministic work, so what varies is exactly the arrival-kept residue: a question group's members (fz-kdt.107) and every pair where neither group covers the other (this ticket). The unit gate a_seed_moves_an_arrival_order_the_group_reversal_cannot pins that difference on three arms in three singleton groups -- the shape this ticket owns -- where the reversal is provably the identity.

Measured: arms:reverse moves 8 fixtures' artifacts, an arm seed moves 27. enum_predicate_search, whose two facet-3 pairs your latest comment names, now ABORTS natively under arms:6 (_fz_list_head_int_ref) where reversal left it green -- so the 'benign today only by a correlation the compiler never proved (luck, ARGUED not proven)' reading has an instrument behind it now.

fz-kdt.143 LANDED (d2a5f3510) and CLOSED the "un-dropped narrow arms a split question group re-arms" population; what remains on the corpus is facet 3 alone. The blind-escape census gate now drives arms:1..6 as well as settled, comparing UNORDERED pairs (an arrival-kept facet-3 flip does not register) with per-setting named constants. Base -> head: settled 3 -> 3, arms:1 3 -> 3, arms:2 5 -> 3, arms:3 5 -> 3, arms:4 3 -> 3, arms:5 3 -> 3, arms:6 7 -> 5. Every entry that left was a dispatch_list_head_separates narrow arm a legal permutation seated ahead of its stand-in. THE FIVE THAT REMAIN ARE ALL THIS TICKET'S: the three settled pairs (dispatch_list_head_separates [:false | :true] with [int | :ok | :true]; enum_predicate_search [:false | :nil] with [int | :nil] and [:false | :true] with [int | :ok | :true]) plus two enum_predicate_search pairs only arms:6 reaches: [int | :nil] with [int] and [int | :ok | :true] with [int]. Those two are structurally out of 143's reach: that [int] arm's CALLABLE surface at subject 2 is strictly WIDER than its siblings' (5 lambdas vs 1 at the all? site, 3 vs 1 at any?), so containment runs one way at subject 0 and the other way at subject 2 and nothing stands in for it -- overlap without containment, exactly facet 3. The census gate is now the instrument that sees all five.

DYNAMIC COUNTS, first time on the production path (fz-kdt.144, 0889c0b3a). The tripwire now walks every element of an admitted list against the clause its head answered, so facet 3 has a runtime instrument. Measured, 597 fixtures, interp: BOTH named settled fixtures read 0 at the settled arrival. dispatch_list_head_separates reads 0 at EVERY setting: Enum.all? folds through List.reduce_while_cont([head | tail], acc, r), which hands the TAIL to the recursive dispatch, so the whole [true, 1, :ok] never reaches a dispatch and what arrives at the [:false | :true] arm is [false] and []. Its header is corrected. The pair is STATICALLY REAL and DYNAMICALLY UNREACHED -- keep that distinction: the seat is still unsafe, the corpus just does not exercise it. enum_predicate_search reads 1 under arms:6: [1, :ok], element 1 = :ok, into a [integer] body -- the pair reached by a real value, and the reproducer to build the cure against; the two arms:6-only pairs named on 143's comment are the same shape. Pinned in SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS (enum_predicate_search settled 0, arms:6 1) so the cure is red-first: it must take that 1 to 0.

HEADS-UP from the fz-kdt.183 cold review (2026-09-03): once recursive keys carry a ground list element, the static blind-escape census EMPTIES (3 -> 0) and dispatch_list_head_separates -- added by fz-kdt.107 step 3 as this ticket's only source-level reproducer -- no longer reproduces its class (element precision keys the three arms apart). Decide on THIS ticket whether the fixture is rewritten to defeat element precision (a facet-3 pair that survives a ground element: overlap without containment at the head with the tails erased) or whether the loss is recorded here; a silent census edit is not the answer. Also: the same change retires every live surface-membership escape on the dynamic census (00277 12 -> 0, enum_predicate_search under arms:6 1 -> 0), so this ticket's dynamic instrument would read zero too -- the population moves to the callable slot (fz-kdt.189).

fz-kdt.178 (8de517a28): the call-edge population is unchanged (3 at the settled arrival: dispatch_list_head_separates 1, enum_predicate_search 2) but it is no longer the whole census -- 45 reachable readings are wrapper selections owned by fz-kdt.179, and the constants are split so your three stay legible (BLIND_ESCAPE_POPULATION keyed by site). Under arms:6, only ONE of the two extra pairs is reachable (`[int | :ok | :true] with [int]`, executable 203); `[int | :nil] with [int]` at executable 201 is separated at another subject and is fz-kdt.186's fiction. Entry, case and receive plans are the source-order census class (0 over the readable ones) and are excluded from the seat law because clause order is the programmer's.

DECISION NEEDED (fz-kdt.183 rule review, 2026-09-03): under 183's demand-through-forwarding rule the static blind-escape population 48 -> 29 with 0 new; the 19 retired include dispatch_list_head_separates (List.reduce_while_step/3 splits into list(int) / list(:false|:true) / list(int|:ok) / list(int|:ok|:true), so the pair a head cannot separate now separates by KEY) and both enum_predicate_search entries -- i.e. this ticket's only source-level reproducer and both corpus facet-3 pairs leave the census. Either re-home the reproducer on a shape a ground element does not separate (a head overlap with erased tails inside ONE key: a callable-fed accumulator, fz-kdt.165's residue) or record here that facet 3 is measured empty at that landing. Not a silent census edit.

fz-kdt.186 landed (accb5cfbe): under arms:6 the seed adds ONE facet-3 pair, not two. `[int | :nil]` with `[int]` at enum_predicate_search executable 201 is separated outright (its callable questions name disjoint closure sets) and is no longer a reading; `[int | :ok | :true]` with `[int]` at executable 203 is your reproducer under that seed. BLIND_ESCAPE_PAIRS_UNDER_SEED_SIX is 49. Your facet-3 class is otherwise unchanged (3 call-edge entries at the settled arrival) -- and fz-kdt.183 empties it (see the decision request above).

title: Runtime-dispatch predicates that overlap without covering either body leave representation safety to arrival order
